key_insight: The paper shows that loss-tolerant fusion-network interfaces can enable distributed lattice surgery for surface codes with high erasure tolerance, reaching a 50% interface-erasure threshold in low-noise regimes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path for networking matter-based QPUs using photonic links while preserving fault-tolerant logical operations across noisy, lossy interfaces.
method: Used ZX-calculus transformations to derive hybrid syndrome-extraction protocols.
Applied the protocols to distributed rotated surface-code lattice surgery with Bell-pair, fused, and linear-cluster-state interfaces.
Analyzed thresholds under resource-state truncation, local circuit noise, fusion erasure, and photon loss, including fusion boosting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 50% interface-erasure thresholds for several protocols when local noise is absent, and maps how thresholds degrade under realistic resource-state and circuit errors.
watch_item: The interface-distance advantage is largely masked at local and resource-state error rates around 10^-3, so benefits may require substantially lower local noise to matter in practice.
paper_title: Loss-tolerant distributed lattice surgery using fusion networks
